BUY-SELL AGREEMENT
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

PURPOSE
This agreement restricts the transfer of ownership interests in Acme, Inc. and sets out what happens to an owner's interest when a triggering event occurs, so the remaining owners and the departing owner's interest don't end up governed only by whatever the default rule happens to be.

TRIGGERING EVENTS
This agreement applies when any of the following happens to an owner:

☐ Death
☐ Permanent disability
☐ Divorce or legal separation affecting ownership of the interest
☐ Voluntary withdrawal or resignation
☐ Involuntary termination or expulsion (as permitted by the company's governing documents)
☐ Bankruptcy or insolvency
☐ A bona fide offer from an outside buyer the owner wishes to accept
☐ Other: _______________________________________________

RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL
Before an owner may transfer an interest to anyone outside the company in response to an outside offer, the owner must first offer that interest to Acme, Inc. and then to the other owners, on the same price and terms as the outside offer. The company and the other owners have _______ days to accept the offer before the owner may proceed with the outside transfer.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN LLC
Without an agreement like this one, a transfer of an LLC membership interest — by sale, gift, or on an owner's death — doesn't by itself dissolve the company or give the person who receives the interest a vote or a role in managing it. That person generally only receives the right to whatever distributions the original owner would have received.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-30]
  "A transfer does not by itself cause a member’s dissociation or a dissolution and winding up of the activities of a limited liability company."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17705.02(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, effect of a transfer (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17705.02.)
  "a transfer does not entitle the transferee to do any of the following: (A) Vote or otherwise participate in the management or conduct of the activities of a limited liability company."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17705.02(a)(3) (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, a transferee doesn't get management rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17705.02.)
  "A transferee has the right to receive, in accordance with the transfer, distributions to which the transferor would otherwise be entitled"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17705.02(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, a transferee's economic rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17705.02.)
  Known gap: This is one state's default rule, used here as real evidence of what happens automatically if the company's own governing documents don't set a different rule — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific company. This default cuts both ways: it's reassuring in that an unplanned transfer doesn't hand a stranger a vote, but it also means the remaining owners can end up running the business alongside someone who has an economic stake but no say and no obligation to contribute, unless this agreement — or the operating agreement itself — sets up a mechanism to convert that situation into an actual buyout.

MAKING THE RESTRICTION STICK FOR AN LLC
For this restriction to actually bind an outside buyer or an owner's heirs — not just the owners who signed it — it needs to be written into Acme, Inc.'s operating agreement, not left as a side agreement. A transfer that violates a restriction written into the operating agreement is ineffective against anyone who had notice of the restriction at the time of the transfer. The company also doesn't have to give effect to a transferee's rights under that same statute until it has actual notice that the transfer happened.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-30]
  "A transfer of a transferable interest in violation of a restriction on transfer contained in the operating agreement is ineffective as to a person having notice of the restriction at the time of transfer."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17705.02(f) (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, a transfer restriction binds a transferee with notice (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17705.02.)
  "A limited liability company need not give effect to a transferee’s rights under this section until the limited liability company has notice of the transfer."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17705.02(e) (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, the company need not recognize a transfer without notice (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17705.02.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of a genuine mechanism — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific LLC. The practical implication: a right of first refusal that lives only in this standalone agreement, and isn't also incorporated into the operating agreement itself, may not bind a transferee who never saw this agreement and had no notice of it. This document is meant to work alongside the operating agreement, not replace it.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR A CORPORATION
If Acme, Inc. is a corporation, this transfer restriction only binds someone who buys or receives shares without knowing about it if the restriction is noted conspicuously on the stock certificate or the written statement that takes its place.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-30]
  "The fact that the shares are subject to restrictions upon transfer."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 418(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California General Corporation Law, required disclosure of a transfer restriction (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=418.)
  "Unless stated on the certificate, the initial transaction statement, and written statements as required by subdivision (a), no restriction upon transfer, no right of redemption and no voting agreement under subdivision (a) of Section 706, no irrevocable proxy under subdivision (e) of Section 705, and no voting restriction imposed by the corporation shall be enforceable against a transferee of the shares without actual knowledge of such restriction, right, agreement or proxy."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 418(b) (California Legislative Information text), California General Corporation Law, enforceability against a transferee without notice (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=418.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of a genuine formal requirement — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific corporation. A transfer restriction that exists only in this agreement or the bylaws, without also appearing on the actual shares or share records, risks being unenforceable against someone who buys or receives those shares without actual knowledge of the restriction.

IF THE CORPORATION IS A CLOSE CORPORATION
If Acme, Inc. has formally elected close corporation status, there's a separate, stricter rule beyond the general transfer-restriction disclosure above: a close corporation's shares must carry a specific legend on their face capping the number of shareholders of record (a number the corporation sets, up to a statutory maximum), and any voluntary transfer that would push the shareholder count past that cap is void — not just unenforceable against an unknowing buyer, but void outright.

[Verified — checked 2026-08-30]
  "All certificates representing shares of a close corporation shall contain in addition to any other statements required by this section, the following conspicuous legend on the face thereof: “This corporation is a close corporation. The number of holders of record of its shares of all classes cannot exceed ____ [a number not in excess of 35]. Any attempted voluntary inter vivos transfer which would violate this requirement is void. Refer to the articles, bylaws and any agreements on file with the secretary of the corporation for further restrictions.”"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 418(c) (California Legislative Information text), California General Corporation Law, required close-corporation legend and shareholder cap (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=418.)
  "Any attempted voluntary inter vivos transfer of the shares of a close corporation which would result in the number of holders of record of its shares exceeding the maximum number specified in its articles is void if the certificate contains the legend required by subdivision (c)."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 418(d) (California Legislative Information text), California General Corporation Law, a transfer past the cap is void (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=418.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of a genuine formal requirement for a specific corporate subtype — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific corporation, and it only applies if the corporation has actually elected close corporation status, which most small corporations have not; whether that election was made is stated in the corporation's own articles of incorporation.

VALUATION
The purchase price for an owner's interest under this agreement will be determined by:

☐ A fixed price of $_______, to be updated by the owners at least annually
☐ The formula: _______________________________________________
☐ An independent appraisal, with the appraiser selected as follows: _______________________________________________

FUNDING THE PURCHASE
The purchase price will be paid as follows:

☐ In full at closing
☐ In installments over _______ months/years, with interest at _______%
☐ From the proceeds of a life insurance policy on the departing owner (if the triggering event is death)
☐ Other: _______________________________________________

SIGNATURES
Agreed to by all current owners:

Owner: _______________________ Date: _______________
Owner: _______________________ Date: _______________
Owner: _______________________ Date: _______________
(Add additional signature lines as needed.)

—
